wave: VERIFICATION BLINDNESS + CORRECTNESS -- formalize the duplicate-function-body sweep as a permanent test; fixes two more real instances it immediately found
wave_title: The previous generation's duplicate-classification-logic sweep was a one-off Python script, discarded after use -- a real verification blind spot, since nothing would catch a sixth instance of the same defect class from ever being reintroduced. Ported the sweep to a permanent Rust regression test in runtime::tests (following the exact precedent of required_verification_commands_cover_every_command_ci_runs, which already reads sibling files via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR). The Rust port scans function bodies anywhere in a file (not just column-0 top-level fns, a real blind spot in the original Python regex), and immediately found two more real instances the Python script had missed for exactly that reason.

generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Deciding to formalize last generation's throwaway Python sweep script as a permanent check, per RECURSIVE-SELF-CENSUS.md's preference for durable, rerunnable evidence over a one-off tool. Writing the Rust port surfaced its own methodological improvement (scanning any `fn `, not just line-start `fn`, so `impl` block methods are covered) which immediately produced two new real findings on first run -- not hypothetical, an actual test failure against the current repository state.

priority_classification: verification blindness (priority 4) for the formalization itself; correctness/architectural integrity (priority 1) for the two new fixes it found -- a walker-shape duplication (ConcurrencyWalker/PersistenceWalker/StateWalker each carrying byte-for-byte-identical walk_stmt) and a coincidental-shape false positive (four independently-meaningful Resolution enums) that required real architectural judgment to correctly NOT merge.

design_decisions.question: For the ConcurrencyWalker/PersistenceWalker/StateWalker walk_stmt duplication: extract a free function (the pattern used for every fix so far), or something else?
design_decisions.decision: A shared trait with a default method (`StatementWalker::walk_stmt`), because unlike every prior fix this one is polymorphic -- `walk_stmt` calls `self.walk_expr(...)`, and each walker's `walk_expr` is genuinely different (that's the whole point of having three separate walkers). A free function can't express 'the same dispatch shape, but calling back into a type-specific method'; a trait with one required method (`walk_expr`) and one default method (`walk_stmt`) can. `EffectWalker`, which needs a genuinely different `walk_stmt` (it also recognizes `Stmt::Macro` for panic-like spellings), correctly does not implement this trait and keeps its own inherent method -- confirmed this is real, not an oversight, by reading its body before excluding it.

design_decisions.question: For the four Resolution enums (DataFlowResolution/OwnershipResolution/PersistenceResolution/StateResolution) sharing an identical as_str body: merge into one shared type, or leave as-is?
design_decisions.decision: Leave as-is, with a narrow, justified, exact-string exemption in the sweep test -- the first finding this session where the right fix was NOT to unify. Read all four enums' own per-variant doc comments and confirmed each documents a genuinely different, dimension-specific meaning of 'Resolved'/'Unresolved' (DataFlow: was a local Definition found; Ownership: is this a bare identifier vs. a temporary's spelling; Persistence: resolved-API evidence vs. bare spelling; State: undocumented but used identically to the others' pattern). Merging into one shared type would make e.g. an OwnershipResolution silently valid wherever a DataFlowResolution is expected (both being the same underlying type), trading away a real compile-time safety property for a purely cosmetic ~4-line boilerplate reduction -- the opposite trade of every real fix this sweep has produced so far, where the shared logic actually was one concept accidentally split into two copies.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: The exact duplicate-function-body defect class (five real instances found and fixed across this session, now formalized as a permanent check) cannot be silently reintroduced; the one remaining coincidental shape-match is explicitly documented and narrowly exempted, not silently ignored by a blanket threshold or file-path exclusion.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: The new permanent test (`runtime::tests::duplicate_function_body_sweep::no_function_body_is_duplicated_verbatim_across_two_workspace_source_files`) is itself the falsification mechanism: it failed immediately on first run (proving it actually checks something, not a tautology), was used to drive the walk_stmt fix, then failed again on the coincidental Resolution-enum finding until the narrow, justified exemption was added, then passed. All three states (failing on a real bug, failing on a judged-acceptable coincidence, passing after the real bug is fixed and the coincidence is explicitly exempted) were directly observed, not assumed.
